meta.title: Muse media
meta.description:
Generate images and video in the conversation with your own Muse account. The plugin drives the Chrome already installed on your machine over CDP and leaves your everyday browser profile alone.

In mainland China, open muse.ai on this computer before installing. Sign in and try the feature you need. If the site stays blank, check connectivity. If Muse reports a region restriction, the feature requires an eligible account in a supported region. Test video separately from images.

**What it does**: three tools. `muse_draw_image` for text-to-image, or image-to-image when you pass `image`, up to 10 references. `muse_draw_video` for text-to-video, or pass `image` as the first frame — Muse honours only the first one. `muse_quota` reads the plan name, this week's used percentage, the next reset and the extra allowance.

**How to use it**: Settings → Muse, then "New account" → "Open sign-in window" and sign in to muse.ai once in the Chrome window that appears. After that, just ask in the conversation. The settings page has three panes: Accounts for the allowance and switching, History for past generations and what each cost, Advanced for browser and timeout values (applied immediately, no restart).

**How an account is chosen**: with several accounts, the one whose **weekly allowance resets soonest** runs first — that allowance is lost on reset while extra credits never expire, so the expiring one is spent first. The pill beside the composer shows `Muse · 25% weekly · acc-01`. While idle that is the account you are looking at; the next generation may pick another, and the tooltip says so.

**Limits**: every generation really spends that account's Muse allowance, exactly as clicking in the web UI would. The same prompt produces a different result twice — there is no seed upstream and the plugin does not offer one. A rate limit or an exhausted allowance stops the task; the plugin will not quietly switch accounts to work around it, with one exception: an expired sign-in. Delivered media is never deleted automatically, because it cost allowance and is referenced by the message that announced it; clearing happens only when you choose "Clear downloaded media". Concurrent browsers are capped (2 by default) since one headless Muse page uses about 1 GB of memory.

**Boundaries**: it drives only the browser you installed and opens a debugging port on loopback only. On exit it closes only the processes it started. It does not provide proxying, daily check-ins, a standalone media library, FFmpeg, canvas, or batch tooling, and it does not use Muse's chat model. Bytes are stored exactly as Muse returned them — no transcoding, no resizing. This plugin spends only Muse allowance and neither affects nor calls any other installed image or video plugin.

**Requirements**: Chrome, Chromium, or Edge on the machine, and your own free Muse account. No browser is bundled.
